By Simon Smale

By Henry Hanson

Topic:Cricket

Australia endured another torrid day in Darwin. (Getty Images: Albert Perez/CA)

Australia's much-vaunted bowling attack has been ground into the Darwin dirt, experiencing another torrid day against Bangladesh at Marrara Stadium.

Led by a sparkling maiden Test ton to rookie-opener Tanzid Hasan, Bangladesh lost just five wickets on day two, reaching stumps on 6-351 and 153 first-innings runs ahead of their hosts.

After an opening day that saw Australia bowled out for a well below-par 198, Pat Cummins's men picked up where they left off on day two, struggling for ideas and inspiration against a disciplined Bangladeshi batting line-up.

Mitchell Starc took the only wicket in an energy-sapping morning session for Australia, while Steve Smith was uncharacteristically slow in reacting to a deflected Tanzid edge, that, if taken, would have seen the opener depart for 62.

Tanzid, playing just his second Test match, took 188 balls to reach his century, and brought it up with a push back past Nathan Lyon after a nervous period in the 90s.

Tanzid completed a sparkling maiden century on day two. (Getty Images: Robert Cianflone)

However, the 25-year-old threw his wicket away only a matter of balls later, caught in the deep after mistiming an ill-advised slog against Lyon for 101.

That was the only wicket to fall in the second session as captain Najmul Hossain Shanto, who had shared a 93-run partnership with Tanzid, continued to take the fight to the Australians alongside 39-year-old, 103-Test veteran Mushfiqur Rahim.

Bangladesh's lead by the time the new ball was taken stood at 91, with seven wickets remaining.

Starc instantly got the new ball talking, sending the first ball swinging past the bat and stumps of Shanto to the giant left hander's complete disbelief.

But it was Hazlewood who made the breakthrough in his first over, finding the edge of Shanto to have him caught at second slip by Steve Smith for 84.

Starc got in on the act three overs later, having Litton Das caught behind, also by Smith, for a 12-ball duck.

Then Pat Cummins joined the party to find the edge of Mushfiqur, and give Smith a third consecutive catch, Australia's three great pacemen striking with fearsome force to reduce Bangladesh from 3-297 to 6-308.

That third catch put Smith level with Joe Root on 218 catches, the most ever in Test cricket by a non wicketkeeper.

But Australia once again toiled as the lacquer faded from the new ball, with six-wicket hero from day one, Hasan Mahmud (13 not out), providing able support to all-rounder Mehidy Hasan Miraz, who reached stumps on 32.

Relive the action in our live blog below.

By Simon Smale

Thanks for the blog Simon and Henry. I had hoped for a competitive game but not necessarily with the Aussies on the ropes after day two! See you tomorrow for a remarkable turnaround in Australia's fortunes...

- Mike

Good day’s work from yourself and Henry , Simon. Beats the hell out of tv commentary which I turn off .

- Phillip

So happy to see Bangladesh doing well n give the complacent Aussies a wake up call.

- Mark

As I said in that final post, this has been a proper day of Test cricket, and Bangladesh have been absolutely brilliant throughout.

Thanks to you all for being with us today, it's been a great game so far and a real contest.

Lets see how it plays out when we return tomorrow.

From myself and Henry, good night.

By Simon Smale

"They batted really well," Jake Weatherald tells Fox Sports.

"We obviously missed a few chances too, but credit to them, they batted really well."

The Aussie batter says that it's clear the pitch has got easier to bat on and that is something he and his teammates are looking forward to do.

"Obviously the wicket's changed quite a lot from our first innings compared to today," he says.

"We're excited to get out there, it looks like a really good track to bat on now.

"I'll go out with the intention to go out and score as quick as I can."

He notes that he's not going to be giving the bowlers any advice, and that the bowlers bowled "really well".

"They feel like they're doing the right things, but obviously they've batted very well."

Key Event

By Simon Smale

Incredible day for Bangladesh once more.

England only managed to keep Australia in the field for more than 100 overs once during the Ashes.

Bangladesh have done so at the first attempt here, and are fully deserving of doing so.

This is proper Test match cricket, and proper Test match batting from the Bangladesh team.

There was a brief flurry of frenetic batting among the Bangladeshi players during that new ball period.

But Mehidy Hasan Miraz 
and Hasan Mahmud have been superb. Brilliant batting.

By Simon Smale

I mean, at this stage, why not.

Mehidy fends into the covers but there is no run there.

Mehidy swipes across the line to fine leg - he turns down the run again.

Gully, second slip, fly slip and bat pad in place as Marnus bowls a bouncer from around the wicket that bounces around half way down the pitch, Ugly delivery that was well ducked under.

Solid defence from Mehidy.

Over the wicket again from Marnus, changing the angle.

CLOSE! Was that a chance? Mehidy cuts to gully and Green drops it!

Oh that's poor, Cam Green should be taking those, just back on his heels.

Cam Green has dropped Mehidy on 32, off the last ball of the day.

By Simon Smale

Nathan Lyon comes back into the attack.

Bat pad and a slip the two close catchers, Mehidy defends the first couple.

Now he dabs a fuller ball down towards mid on. Why is mid on half way back? Bring him up, present an option for the batter to attempt a hit over the top. Lyon's one big weakness for me, his poor field placements.

Hasan defends the first couple of balls he faces from the GOAT in this spell.

Solid defence ends the over.

By Simon Smale

Mehidy is standing square on to Marnus, and he wants to hook the ball but Marnus puts a yorker in. Fended away.

Mehidy stands square again, Marnus bowls outside off and it's left alone.

EDGED! Past the keeper to fly slip for a single! I think he tried to play it that way, Mehidy.

Hasan ducks under a bouncer as second slip comes in, first is vacant and the fly slip goes deeper even towards a backstop type position.

Hasan fends a ball that Marnus bowls pretty well.

Not a bad over there from Marnus, just a single off that outside edge against it.

By Simon Smale

Is this what "Hold a tiger by the tail" means?

- Mike

By Simon Smale

Mehidy has to present the straightest of bats to see out a ball that's aimed at the stumps from Cummins.

Another ball on the poles, another big bat face stopping it from crashing into them.

Single for Mehidy.

Hasan defends solidly.

Bouncer, Hasan gets low and the ball follows him towards the leg side, fading away over his back.

Hasan is rapped on the pads, the slip cordon go up, Cummins turns around dismissively as he knows full well that ball was going a long way down leg and was not worth appealing for.

By Simon Smale

Goodness me. Well, it's worth a shot, I guess.

But if anything else says that Australia has run out of ideas more than this, please let me know.

Bouncer from Marnus, 125km/h. I assume he's on to try and talk the batters out as much as bowl them out.

Mehidy pulls another short one and it's a single down to fine leg.

Fly slip, gully, deep bat pad. Weird field for a weird man. Bouncer again, Hasan ducks under it.

A slip comes in. Another bouncer that Hasan gets under.

BEATEN! Oh don't do that, Hasan, you'll only encourage him. Marnus wheels away as he gets one to swing past the outside edge.

By Simon Smale

I think we had Captain Pat saving the day on our bingo card... get those pens ready...

Bouncer that Carey can't gather as it drops down in front of him. No run, no shot offered.

A single for Mehidy, just keeping the strike moving through.

Hasan defends solidly into the off side.

BEATEN! A ripper from Captain Pat. Just moved a bit off the deck away from Hasan, who played down the line and the ball flew past the outside edge. Good ball, there is still life in this pitch.

Hasan defends a rising ball outside off.

Solid defence ends the over, Cummins saving the fastest for last, 135km/h.

By Simon Smale

Pat Cummins is warming up. He might be replacing Starc after that little outburst.

Mehidy leaves the first and drives the second to long off and takes the single.

Mehidy is saying "I didn't see" to the umpire, perhaps still to do with Starc's frustrations. I don't think I'd be so apologetic - let the Aussies stew. They're the ones who are not firing. I'd keep stirring the pot, I think.

Hasan defends solidly.

Solid defence again, Webster in the holding pattern job.

EDGED!! Hasan has a swing! Was there an edge? There might have been you know?! Yes there was, and it dropped just short of Carey, who couldn't dive forward far enough to grab the ball on the full (but he did brilliantly to gather it on the bounce in fairness).

By Simon Smale

FOUR! Great shot! Gorgeous drive through the covers, and Jake Weatherald chased hard, dived, but couldn't get there. It's a lovely shot, just a fraction of width from Starc and Mehidy punished it.

Another drive, squarer and less fiercely struck this time, no run taken.

Well wide from Starc, Mehidy was a bit interested to have a swipe, but he'd have fallen over had he reached that far to get bat to it.

Another wide ball from Starc, this time Mehidy does reach and does get bat on it, and they run a single.

"It's my follow through, not your follow through. Get off the wicket," Starc says to Mehidy after they nearly collide. Starc fired up, and annoyed at the way his team  has played no doubt.

Starc sees the last ball of the over fended away, and he's losing his cool a bit, the big left hander, who should know better, as he chirps again at Mehidy, who will be loving every verbal barb. He's got under Starc's skin.

By Simon Smale

Change of bowling, Beau Webster getting a chance to bowl and keep things tight. He's been OK today with the ball, 0-26 off 8 overs so far.

Mehidy is fending the ball away, only 120km/h there or there abouts, so not quick, but very accurate.

Short and wide, Mehidy cuts the ball to point for a single.

Better accuracy again there from Webster, back on the money, as Hasan has to defend off his stumps.

He leaves outside off.

Good ball from Webster, the ball angling in as Hasan defends solidly. He's faced 54 balls now for his 13 runs, the Aussies being made to work.

By Simon Smale

Looks like Bangladesh are playing the opposite of Bazball out there, calm set of heads knuckling down, who would have thought that would work in Australia?

- Doc

By Simon Smale

It's the 20th over he has bowled in this innings - few times has Starc had to get through as much work in the first innings as he has today in the first innings of a Test match on home soil.

Mehidy shoulders arms as left handed Starc comes around the wicket, angling the ball in to the right handed batter.

Three slips still, and a gully, the rest of the field is spread, as Mehidy pushes square to backward point but, once again, Mehidy doesn't fancy running. He is 19 off 43 balls, Hasan Mahmud is 11 off 48.

EDGED! Great stop from Marnus Labuschagne at third slip - they take a single but it should have been a boundary. I may have done Mehidy a disservice there as he played for that, an extraordinarily late cut that was angled through the slips. Great stop from Marnus.

Bouncer from Starc at 144km/h, Hasan ducks under it.

Down the leg side from Starc, Hasan gets out the way and Carey takes a good grab down that leg side.

Hasan clips off his pads, a yorker from Starc, a couple of runs to Hasan and Bangladesh.

By Simon Smale

He has to do this, Nathan Lyon, just hold an end and be a threat for as long as he can.

Mehidy defends the first couple.

Make that the first three.

This is a good battle, this. I'd love to see Lyon start to think about setting a trap, which I have no doubt he is doing, only imperceptible to eyes as uneducated as mine.

Mehidy releases the pressure with a clip to midwicket for a couple.

Now he pushes into the off side and gets a single to point.

Hasan clips the last away to square leg but won't take a single, even as Travis Head jogs backward before picking the ball up.

By Simon Smale

Just a three-over spell for Cameron Green, who goes back to gully after a fruitless handful of deliveries.

Wide across the face of Mehidy, who leaves well alone. "Oh, Mitchell," cries Marnus Labuschagne.

Three slips, the third a little wider than orthodox, and a gully as Starc tries to get on off the outside edge. It's not tempting him yet.

Now Mehidy drives into the off side, no run there though as cover fields.

Starc is showing no ill effects from the slip he had on the turf when taking the catch of Tanzin off Nathan Lyon earlier in the day. That's a good thing.

He's also dispensed with the headband he was wearing yesterday. That's a good thing, too.

Mehidy clips off his pads for a single to backward square leg and they will take a single.

Outside off, Hasan plays inside the line, provoking a smidgin of excitement from the slip cordon, but it was brief, as Starc grimaces after loosening up after his first over back.

By Simon Smale

Hasan defends solidly into the off side.

He defends with a very straight bat now, back down the pitch.

Carey gives a half-hearted "come on Gaz," as Lyon comes in once more, Mehidy defends.

Two slips and a bat pad in place as Lyon comes around the wicket to the right hander - I'm not sure there's enough turn for this tactic, can he get one to grip just enough to test Hasan's resolve? Not yet, it seems.

That over is solidly and comfortably seen out, a maiden for Lyon.

By Simon Smale

Mehidy defends the first and leaves the second.

This pair, Hasan and Mehidy have really settled things down for Bangladesh. There was a bit of freneticism with the new ball, panic almost, as wickets fell, but now it's settled down. The partnership is 22 from 65 balls.

Fly slip in place now, two orthodox slips and a gully. Only the one ball though as Mehidy fends away to backward point for a single.

Two slips and a gully and Lyon back on the rope now at deep cover, Hasan leaves well alone.

Green sends another one wide outside off, not a threat, not really doing anything to be honest, the Western Australian.

Driven nicely out to deep cover, just a single to end the over.
